summary: Our project is an interactive Martian surface navigation and mission planning platform built for human and robotic Mars exploration. Powered by real NASA MOLA topographic data, it features a 3D WebGL globe with 4K surface textures, real-time elevation displacement, and a complementary 2D cartographic view. An intelligent spherical A* pathfinder navigates between authentic landing sites, routing around extreme slopes, high-altitude radiation zones, and crater rims while optimizing energy consumption. The platform includes an interactive rocker-bogie traversal simulator with live wheel physics and dynamic pitch tilt, alongside mission-critical telemetry displaying speed, distance, elevation profiles, Sol time, power draw, and hazard ratings for safe Martian expedition planning.
details:
1. What does it do or how does it work?

6S-INSTINCT // MARTIAN MAP is an interactive, browser-based planetary navigation and mission-planning platform designed for Martian surface traversal.

  • Spherical Pathfinding Engine: Users select origin and destination sites (from 20+ authentic historical landing sites or custom coordinates). The routing engine uses a spherical A* corridor algorithm that samples NASA MOLA topographic data across 3D Great-Circle SLERP paths and perpendicular lateral corridors (up to 600 km wide).
  • Multi-Tier Hazard Avoidance: The algorithm calculates slope gradients, penalizes steep inclines, imposes an impassable barrier on slopes >25∘>25∘ to prevent vehicle rollover, and avoids altitudes >3,500 m>3,500 m to reduce cosmic radiation exposure.
  • Physics-Based Traversal Simulation: Features an interactive 2D rocker-bogie vehicle simulation that rolls with physical wheel-ground contact directly over the true MOLA elevation cross-section, calculating dynamic chassis pitch, Sol timeline, speed, and power draw (kW).
  • Dual-View Cartography: Seamlessly toggles between an interactive 3D WebGL globe with 4K surface and displacement textures, and a high-performance 2D GIS map.

2. What benefits does it have?

  • Zero Blind Spots: Solves the challenge of navigating without Martian GPS by using open-source planetary datasets to provide accurate distances, travel times (Sols), and energy metrics.
  • Mission Safety & Rollover Prevention: By actively penalizing steep slopes and treacherous crater rims, routes prioritize mission survival over sheer straight-line distance.
  • Energy & Battery Optimization: Incorporates gravitational work (W=m⋅g⋅ΔhW=m⋅g⋅Δh) into its cost function, ensuring rovers and pressurized astronaut carriers travel through energy-efficient valley corridors rather than draining power on unnecessary ascents.
  • Instant Accessibility: 100% client-side web application with zero backend latency—runs smoothly on any modern desktop, tablet, or mobile browser.

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

  • Future Human Mars Expeditions: Serves as a tactical navigation and logistics planner for astronauts planning Extravehicular Activities (EVAs) and pressurized carrier sorties between habitats and science outposts.
  • Robotic Surface Exploration: Provides path planning architectures that can be adapted for autonomous on-rover navigation systems, reducing reliance on Earth-to-Mars communication delays (4 to 24 minutes).
  • STEM & Public Engagement: Offers students, researchers, and space enthusiasts an accessible, visually stunning tool to explore the topography and geography of Mars through real NASA data.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

  • Languages & Core Frameworks: TypeScript, React 18, HTML5 Canvas API, CSS3.
  • 3D Planetary Graphics & WebGL: Three.js, react-globe.gl (with custom shader displacement, directional sun lighting, and 4K planetary sphere mapping).
  • 2D Mapping & GIS: Leaflet, OpenStreetMap / Mars tile layers.
  • Styling & UI Components: Tailwind CSS, Lucide React icons, Google Fonts (Poppins & JetBrains Mono with tabular numeral alignment).
  • Build Tools & Hosting: Vite, Node.js, Netlify (Continuous Deployment / Static Hosting).
  • Datasets: NASA Mars Orbiter Laser Altimeter (MOLA) topographic data, USGS / NASA Viking MDIM 2.1 global color mosaics.

. How is your project creative?

  • Hill-Climb Style 2D Cross-Section Simulator: Instead of merely displaying static 2D elevation charts, we transformed terrain profiles into a playable, interactive 2D rocker-bogie simulation with suspension tilt and dust dynamics, allowing mission planners to visually "feel" the steepness of every crater and ridge.
  • Monochrome Deep-Space Design Language: Designed with a focused Charcoal & White palette and monospace tabular telemetry, avoiding cartoonish clutter to mirror real aerospace Mission Control consoles.
  • Dynamic Lateral Corridor Beam-Search: Adapts Euclidean grid pathfinding into spherical planetary coordinate space, balancing great-circle tracks with wide lateral sweeps around planetary-scale volcanic domes.

6. What factors did your team consider?

  • Planetary Curvature & Non-Euclidean Geometry: Traditional flat-grid pathfinding distorts near polar regions; our system computes spherical haversine distances and spherical linear interpolation (SLERP).
  • Atmospheric & Radiation Hazards: We accounted for the Martian atmospheric pressure drop at elevations >3,500 m>3,500 m (<1 mbar<1 mbar), penalizing high volcanic peaks where thin atmosphere drastically elevates ionizing cosmic radiation exposure.
  • Rover Mechanical Constraints: Physical limits of 6-wheel rocker-bogie mobility systems informed our slope thresholds (safe driving <12∘<12∘; hard refusal >25∘>25∘).
  • Mars Timekeeping: Converted journey metrics into true Martian Sols (~24.6 hours) assuming realistic 4-hour daily driving windows to match rover operational constraints.
